features.title: One backend for the entire IDC workflow
features.lead: From publishing a product to closing the books, without a second spreadsheet.

items.title: Catalog & pricing
items.desc: Multi-cycle pricing, configurable options, stock and reseller discounts; totals are always recomputed server-side.

items.title: Orders & provisioning
items.desc: Checkout, payment callbacks, upstream provisioning, retries, suspend and release on expiry.

items.title: Finance
items.desc: Balance, top-ups, invoices, refunds, reconciliation and ledger; amounts accumulated in cents.

items.title: Accounts
items.desc: KYC, membership tiers, reseller commissions, payouts and login risk control.

items.title: Tickets
items.desc: Department routing, auto-close on timeout, attachment protection, upstream forwarding.

items.title: Notifications
items.desc: In-app, email and SMS with configurable templates and retries.

items.title: Automation
items.desc: Scheduled jobs, heartbeat monitoring, reconciliation, log archiving.

items.title: Plugins
items.desc: Six plugin families with clear boundaries: swap an upstream without touching the core.

flow.title: One pipeline from checkout to reconciliation
flow.lead: Six stages share the same orders, accounts and ledger; a failed step rolls back, so you never see provisioned-but-unpaid.

security.title: Start with the flaws we don't have
security.lead: The issues commonly reported against commercial IDC systems, each mapped to an implementation you can verify in the repository.

none.title: Price tampering
none.desc: Order and renewal totals are recomputed server-side; client parameters cannot rewrite the amount due.

none.title: Leaked upstream credentials
none.desc: Upstream tokens stay server-side; clients and anonymous requests never receive the raw JWT.

none.title: Arbitrary file upload
none.desc: Uploads require authentication and are validated for type, size and quota.

none.title: Feature gating and backdoors
none.desc: No license checks, no disabled features, no remote control; the code is fully auditable.

none.title: Cross-tenant access
none.desc: Queries and mutations bind to the current owner; violations return 403 / 404.

none.title: Payment replay
none.desc: Idempotent callbacks plus a unique transaction constraint: each payment is booked and fulfilled once.

none.title: Injection and spoofing
none.desc: Parameterized SQL; untrusted proxy headers ignored for client IP; secure cookies and CSRF protection.

have.title: Authoritative server-side math
have.desc: Amounts, stock, coupons and renewals recomputed and locked server-side.

have.title: Complete audit trail
have.desc: Money movements, orders and admin actions are recorded and exportable.

have.title: Login risk control
have.desc: Soft lockouts per account and IP; captcha throttled per target.

have.title: Plugin architecture
have.desc: Six plugin families with explicit boundaries, replaceable end to end.

have.title: Automated fallbacks
have.desc: Scheduling, heartbeats, reconciliation, retries and automatic release.

have.title: Open and auditable
have.desc: AGPL-3.0-or-later: review, patch and extend in the open.

deploy.lead: One codebase: Docker Compose, BaoTa panel or bare metal. Rewrite rules and cron setup ship in the docs.

items.title: Docker Compose

faq.title: What to confirm before going live

items.a: The open-source edition is free under AGPL-3.0-or-later, with no feature gating, no license checks and no backdoors. The full source is auditable.

items.q: Can I run it closed-source commercially?
items.a: That needs the commercial license (CNY 200 / year), which grants terms outside AGPL. Without it, offering the modified system as a service requires sharing the complete corresponding source, including your changes.

items.q: Can I migrate from ZJMF Finance?
items.a: Yes. Products, customers, orders, upstreams and KYC data have documented migration paths and checklists; TuraIDC can also act as an upstream so both systems run in parallel first.

items.q: Which upstreams and payment channels are supported?
items.a: Upstreams, payments, SMS, captcha, KYC and mail are all plugins. ZJMF, KangHostx and EPay ship built in; anything else follows the plugin contract without touching the core.

items.q: What server environment does it need?
items.a: PHP 8.3+ with Laravel 12, MySQL 5.7.8+ (8.0 recommended) and Redis 6+. The three frontends build to static assets served by Nginx. Sizing details are in the deployment docs.

Read the architecture and frontend guidelines first, then pick one business domain. Plugins live in backend/plugins/{domain}/{slug}/; do not add logic to system routes, schedules or global middleware.
